area: correctness / ADR-027 re-arm vs. the documented contract (residual of the claimTerminal fix)
location: Sources/ZTronAssetAppleHosted/PackTransfer.swift:180-182 (forgetRelease inside conclude) vs :168-169 (doc says 'only when a staged copy is delivered') and :186-198 (deliver)
problem: `conclude` claims the terminal, then re-arms the pack's release before `run()` yields anything. Between the claim and the yield there is an actor hop (`await self.parts.state.forgetRelease(pack)`) and `interval.end()`. If the consumer drops the stream in that window, `deliver` sees `.terminated` and discards the staged copy, but the release was already re-armed. So a pack can be released again when no consumer ever received a copy. That contradicts the doc comment at :168-169 and E-10's wording 'only a delivered staged copy re-arms'. PROBE-C1-6 reproduces run()'s exact steps through the `conclude` and `deliver` seams: conclude (staged, downloaded ZTronMedia), consumer task cancelled, deliver, reclaim. It printed 'PROBE-C1-6 copyDelivered=false copyLeft=false released=2 removes=2', so the expectation 'released == 1' failed. The pack is removed and downloaded once more per occurrence. This needs a fresh demand plus a drop in a sub-millisecond window each time, so it is not a loop. That is why it is non-blocking.
fix: Re-arm only after a successful yield. Make `deliver` return whether the terminal was enqueued (`let delivered = !(updates.yield(terminal) is .terminated)`), have `conclude` return the pack to re-arm instead of calling `forgetRelease`, and in `run()` do `if delivered, let pack = rearm { await self.parts.state.forgetRelease(pack) }` after `deliver`. A reclaim that runs between the yield and the forget only skips the pack once (it is still marked released), which is harmless. Alternatively, reword the doc comment and E-10 to say 'claimed' and accept the narrow window. Add PROBE-C1-6 (in .build-verify-e-close-correct1/probes/pkg/Tests/Probe/CloseProbes.swift) as a regression test either way.

area: design / ADR-027 'at most once per pack per catalog generation' (E-10(b) not explicitly ratified)
problem: Re-arming on a staged on-demand copy is by design (E-10(b)). It means an asset that the retention scope excludes, but that its pack does hold, makes the source download the whole pack and remove it again on every request-then-maintenance cycle within one catalog generation. ADR-027 says the store evicts out-of-scope entries first, so this cycle is realistic for out-of-scope assets that are viewed on demand. PROBE-C1-1g (catalog = a adopted + x excluded and present, 4 rounds of transfer x then reclaim, one generation) printed 'PROBE-C1-1g released=5 removes=5 mediaEnsures=4 (one generation)'. ADR-027's decision text says 'at most once per pack per catalog generation'. The close-out rulings ratify E-1, E-4, E-15, E-13 and E-10's in-memory persistence, but not the (b) exception. This is not a regression: the close-out narrowed (b), it did not widen it.
fix: Orchestrator: either ratify E-10(b) as an explicit ADR-027 amendment, accepting a whole-pack re-download per demand after release, or restrict the re-arm to the case (b) was written for. That case is an entry that was adopted in the last surveyed report: keep the adopted remote paths per media pack from `planRelease`, and forget only when `request.remotePath` is among them, never for an excluded-only entry. Add PROBE-C1-1g as a test of whichever behaviour is chosen.
